title: The Hidden Geography of Housing Demand Exposes Policy Failure: Evidence from Billions of Housing Searches
publisher: University of Warwick / CAGE (Datta, Kulka, Wehbe)
key_point: 16bn UK portal searches: 60% use max-price filter; COVID greenspace demand (+0.8%/100m2) reverted to zero by end-2023; Wandsworth high excess demand.

title: Valuing Rail Access Using Transport Innovations (CEP DP 611; JUE 2005)
publisher: LSE Centre for Economic Performance (Gibbons, Machin)
key_point: JLE/DLR stations: prices rise ~1.5-5.8% per km closer to station within 2km; no effect beyond 2km.

title: Valuing School Quality Using Boundary Discontinuities (SERC DP 18; JUE 2013)
key_point: One SD rise in school value-added or prior attainment raises house prices ~3% in England.

title: What are buyers prioritising as mortgage rates rise?
key_point: Garden 74% essential; broadband 90%, amenities 87%, transport 86%, home office 73% essential/important; a third lost spending power.

title: What buyers want most (and least) when purchasing a home
key_point: Broadband 82% top; garden 76%; transport rose 14th to 6th since 2021; square footage fell 2nd to 7th.

title: Home buyers put fresh air and family ahead of proximity to the office
key_point: London: park proximity 57%, garden 50%, home workspace 48%; tube proximity top-two fell 63% to 39%.

title: First-time buyer outlook 2021
key_point: 3,744 FTBs: in London local green space rose most post-COVID, balcony/terrace = outside space, storage outranks parking.

title: London first-time buyers focusing on neighbourhood
key_point: London FTBs: neighbourhood 79% extremely important, bedrooms 48%, transport 43%, outdoor space 43%; >60% prefer new-build.

title: What tops the wish list for London's first time buyers?
key_point: 1,000 London renters 24-35: 76% expect to compromise on location, 50% expect to leave London; transport, amenities, parks top.

title: In search of space: London suburbs 'red hot', says property research firm
key_point: Buyers swapped vertical for lateral space; tube-adjacency premium shrank; Dulwich, Wimbledon, Crouch End hotspots.

title: What's next for the housing market in 2025? Home buyer behaviour and user trends unveiled (Zoopla)
key_point: 80% view floorplans before photos; 'freehold' top keyword, then garage, annexe; 'study' and 'needs modernisation' rising.

title: Homebuyers' most searched-for locations in 2025 revealed
key_point: London most searched; Wimbledon, Fulham, Chiswick top London buyer searches; garage, annexe, garden top buyer keywords.

title: UK's top property hotspots of 2025 revealed
key_point: Confirms Rightmove 2025: buyers' top features garage, annexe, garden; renters pet-friendly; London top location.

title: Homebuyers abandon flats in favour of houses
key_point: Lockdown: 40% changed priorities, 39% want garden/bigger home, 1 in 5 want WFH space; top-5 searched types all houses.

title: London new homes update - February 2025
key_point: London new-home buyers prefer build-complete stock; £500-750k exchanges +20% in 2024; needs-driven buyers dominate.

title: What to consider when buying in Prime Central London
key_point: PCL buyers want community, green space, high street, schools; Westminster caps new lateral flats at 200 sqm.

title: Savills research: school areas price premium
key_point: Top school areas 56% above regional average; London only 82.6% secondary first-choice offers; London/SE dominate.

title: Why London's small flat market crisis runs deeper than the data shows
key_point: ~Half of London 1-bed/studios sell below purchase price; inner London flats -6.2%; service charges, cladding, short leases deter.

title: Soaring service charges on leasehold flats hit capital values
key_point: London service charge £2,801/yr (+41% in 5 yrs); 37% of flats exceed 1% of value; low-charge flats 50% likelier to sell.

title: Flats are falling out of favour
key_point: 73% of FTBs buy houses (65% in 2015); 19.9% of flats sold at loss in 2025, studios 38.1%.

title: Flats offer 'growing value' amid falling demand, says Zoopla
key_point: Flat demand falling on running costs and leasehold; London remains exception with persistent but uncertain flat demand.

title: Lower mortgage rates keep first-time buyers in London: Hamptons
key_point: Record 48% of London sales to FTBs in H1 2024 at avg £443,550; leavers buy ~24 miles out.

title: Downsizers driving London demand for new homes
key_point: Downsizers lead London market; want lateral space, lifts, low bills, estate management, central locations; mostly cash buyers.

title: Barratt London over-50s survey findings
key_point: Over-50 Londoners: outdoor space 51%, green space 63%, parking 37%; only 32% would leave London.

title: Parents face 5% premium on properties within catchment areas of top primary schools
key_point: Catchment premium ~25% in London vs 5% elsewhere; 63% of parents would pay extra (26% in 2019).

title: Property prices double around Elizabeth Line stations
key_point: Elizabeth line 2012-22: Maryland asking prices +108% vs London +55%; buyer demand up to +245%.

title: Top 10 must-haves on buyers' wish lists revealed
key_point: National keyword top 10: garage, annexe, acre, garden, detached, cottage, character, bungalow, freehold, rural.

title: Flat v house (Mumsnet Property)
key_point: 78 replies: flat with big garden, top schools, short commute beats SE London house; 'location first'; leasehold caveats.

title: 400K budget where to buy in London
key_point: Posters push rail-served areas over tube-only; 30-min commute rule too restrictive; Sutton schools/safety cited.

title: Can I still buy in London (Mumsnet AIBU)
key_point: 94 replies on £500-550k 2-bed: drop tube filter, consider Elizabeth/Overground areas; green space, cafes, safety.

title: Where would you spend a third of a million in London
key_point: £300-350k: commute logistics decide area; flats/conversions in outer zones; houses unaffordable.

title: Leave an up and coming area for a house?
key_point: Flat-to-house upsizers weigh station frequency, Travelcard cost, ex-council ceiling; consensus favours moving out for space.

title: North London house buying areas advice
key_point: £500k 2-bed: commute, tube/Overground, villagey feel, safety, green space drive area choice (East Finchley, Alexandra Park).

title: Where in London would you buy?
key_point: £150k SW London unrealistic; trade-offs between safety, condition and commute; Croydon/Isleworth suggested.

title: What buyers want: the top features that will make your home appeal to London househunters
key_point: London Rightmove keywords: garden 1st, freehold 2nd, Help to Buy 3rd, balcony 5th (snippet only).

title: Home counties hotspots where London buyers are snapping up properties revealed
key_point: Londoners buying outside capital 5.3% (12-yr low); 18.2% of Home Counties sales to Londoners (snippet only).

title: First-time buyer numbers up 19% in 2024: Halifax
key_point: UK FTB average age 33, deposit £61,090, price £311,034 in 2024 (snippet only).

title: Rightmove: What homebuyers wanted from the housing market in 2025
key_point: Rightmove 2025 year review of searches (403 on fetch; content matched via MPA/PIE).
